territorial_scope.description: Applies across the United Kingdom, with some provisions specific to England and Wales, Scotland or Northern Ireland; notices may reach entities registered or trading outside the UK, and individual orders and notices name specific persons or service providers.

summary.short: Crime and Policing Act 2026 (UK, dated 29 April 2026) makes provision on anti-social behaviour, offensive weapons, retail crime, child criminal exploitation, cuckooing and police powers across the United Kingdom, with some measures specific to England, Wales, Scotland or Northern Ireland.
summary.long: The Act makes provision on anti-social behaviour, offensive weapons, retail crime, child criminal exploitation and cuckooing, and police powers. Respect orders may be made against persons aged 18 or over; youth injunctions are confined to those aged 10 to 17. Some police directions and closure notices may last longer, and some fixed penalty notice amounts rise from £100 to £500. Part 2 provides for removal of unlawful weapons content from user-to-user and search services, with penalties up to £60,000 for providers and £10,000 for content managers. It creates offences of possessing a bladed article or offensive weapon with intent to use unlawful violence, regulates remote sale and delivery of knives and crossbows, and raises weapons sentences. Part 3 creates an offence of assaulting a retail worker, requires a criminal behaviour order in certain convictions, and makes theft from shops triable either way. Part 4 creates child criminal exploitation and cuckooing offences and CCE prevention orders against persons aged 18 or over. The long title also covers sexual offences, stalking, police and border powers, terrorism and corporate liability; those provisions are not in the text reviewed.

notes: The text supplied is labelled part 1 of 6 but contains ss. 1 to 67 only. Schedules 1 to 9, commencement and extent provisions are not in the text supplied, so schedule-only amendments are noted rather than coded, and the instrument's commencement status cannot be checked from this text. 'Relevant authority' is defined separately for the respect-order Part A1 (s. B1(2)) and for the information power (s. 105A(8), inserted by s. 7), and the two lists differ. The Sentencing Code is referred to without a citation. Part 2 of 6 covers ss. 68 to 128(2) only; provisions after s. 128(5) are not in this part. Relation target_instrument_id values are blank because registry IDs were not supplied; target_text names each instrument. Duplicate mentions of the same act are merged into one row per target. Internal reference check: new s. 86A(5)(a) refers to Schedule 3 paragraphs 35B to 35E, but this part inserts only 35D (via s. 80), so 35E is not inserted here. The Schedule 3 numbering must be checked against other parts. Enabling regulation powers (ss. 68(9), 84, 91, 110, 111, 112(5)) are not coded as relations. Part 3 of 6 covers ss.129 to 204(1); s.204 is cut off at the boundary and continues in part 4. Mainly amendments to other Acts, new offences, orders and powers. No commencement dates are stated in this part; several provisions run from commencement or from specified dates set elsewhere (e.g. ss.137(5), 138(4), 145(8), 200(8), 201(9)). Target instruments are not matched to registry IDs here, so target_instrument_id is left empty. Sec. 133 refers to the Department without defining it in this part. Sec. 153(5) contains a drafting error (a similar to). Sec. 136(5) repeals Online Safety Act 2023 s.184. The text supplied as part 4 of 6 runs from the Police Act 1996 amendments through Schedule 9 and was annotated in full. target_instrument_id is an empty string where the target is not in the registry (no registry IDs were supplied). Commencement is governed by s.255 (regulations or set days, two months after Royal Assent for some sections, and some provisions on Royal Assent); no commencement events are recorded here. Drafting: s.213(3)(b) has an unclosed bracket after section 211 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026. Schedule 9 lists offences from many further Acts (including Scottish Acts); only selected Acts are recorded as relations. Critical police undertakings (s.214) are described by criteria, not named bodies, so no entity is recorded for them. Part 5 of 6 covers the offence list in the Part 3 Northern Ireland section before Schedule 10 (its schedule heading is not in this part and is inferred to be Schedule 9), and Schedules 10 to 21. Schedules 11, 13, 15, 19 and 21 are mainly consequential or amending schedules. Schedules 14, 16, 18 and 21 contain operative powers; Schedule 14's duties on service providers are conferred only through regulations ("may"). New sections such as 8A to 8C of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 are referred to here but are defined outside this part. Schedule 17 lists specified memorials and is not coded. Under the schema, lei and ticker are empty strings where not verified, and target_instrument_id is empty where no registry ID is known. Relations and entities are included under section_status as not_applicable because entries are present. This part covers the text from section 35Q onward, Part 13 and Schedules 22 to 27 as shown. Empty strings are used where no registry ID, LEI or ticker is available. The text refers to both the Sentencing Code and the Sentencing Act 2020 without stating their relationship. Schedule 23 para 2 cites section 249 of the Procedure Act, a term not defined in this text. Section 52 cites section 3 of the Sentencing Act 2026, which is not identified further. Section 53 makes prospective amendments to Schedule 22 of the Sentencing Code without a stated date. Most commencement dates are not stated in this part; several provisions apply from a day to be appointed. Schedule 22 contains Northern Ireland counterparts to several England and Wales provisions.
